steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Mix eggs, bananas, oil, and buttermilk together in a large bowl until well combined.
Sift flour, sugar, baking soda, and salt into a separate large bowl.
Stir flour mixture into the banana mixture until combined. Gently fold in pecans.
Pour batter into the prepared loaf pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then unmold onto a wire rack to cool completely. Cut into slices and enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Best Ever Banana Bread
raw_recipe.description: This best-ever banana bread recipe uses a secret ingredient: buttermilk. It makes this nutty banana bread wonderfully moist and very, very tasty!

review.reviewBody: Seriously.. stop writing reviews of 'best ever' when you changed the entire recipe!!!!!

This is wonderful. Yogurt works as well as buttermilk. I also accidentally found out that if you use vanilla yogurt instead of buttermilk, applesauce instead of oil, and cut out the sugar, it's a pretty good low fat, low sugar treat. Better if it sits for a day so the natural sugars can absorb. I've tweaked this recipe a lot and no matter how I make it it's wonderful! Thanks, Rose!

This is definitely THE BEST banana bread I've ever come across- but I swear I've made it even better. Try this-
Take 4 oz. of room temp cream cheese, beat it together with 3T milk until smooth. Add 1 cup of powdered sugar and 1/2 t. vanilla and mix until incorporated. Drizzle this over your banana bread when it's done, take a bite and you will swear you've died and gone to heaven.

This banana bread lives up to its name as "best banana bread". It freezes perfectly and tasted just as good a week later as when I had just baked it. When I greased the loaf pan, I dusted the pan with sugar. This gave it a crunchy crust with a moist interior. Try this recipe! You won't be disappointed!

For my review I followed the recipe to a T. It came out amazing and if I was the type of person who used a recipe every time I baked I’d tattoo this to the inside of my eyelids! It is moist, has a rich banana taste, has a nice peak after baking, and keeps wonderfully out on the counter with plastic wrap over it (I’ve never had any leftover more than 3 days 😬). Since I love to change recipes to my personal palate this is how I make the bread now… I use 1/2 C white sugar, 1/2 C + approx. 1/8 C brown sugar (plenty of sweetness with this reduced amount of sugar), 2 large or 3 small bananas (I never measure these), 1 tsp vanilla, 1 heaping tsp cinnamon, and since buttermilk is so easy to make I pour about a tsp lemon juice in a 1/3 C measuring cup and then fill with milk and let sit about 10 minutes. I use a little over a C of pecans and a little over a C of mini chocolate chips and fold them in as the last step before pouring into the loaf pan. Btw, if you need a new loaf pan the Great Jones Breadwinner Non-Stick Loaf Pan is amazing! I’ve tried so many and this one is the best. It feel slick on the inside and you’ll never have anything stick to it. So… once I pour the mixture into the pan I throw some cinnamon sugar into a bowl and add chopped pecan pieces, toss the pecans around in the cinnamon sugar and coat the top of the loaf with this. How much you use depends on how crunchy you want the top of the loaf. 1hr and 20 minutes works good for me (may change for you by a few minutes here or there depending on your oven). I dig into it whole it’s still hot because I’m not good waiting 🤪

I have used this recipe well over a decade. Made exactly as is, it IS the best ever 🍌 🍞 recipe I have found.However, depending on what's in the pantry, I may add /take away some ingredients.I use only 1/2 cup white sugar, added to dry mix, and 1/2 cup dark brown added to the wet mixture. I also use 2 1/2 to 3 🍌 sliced as coins. I am going to add some almond extract the next time as per one review.But again, made as posted, this is, in my opinion, the best ever 🍌 bread recipe. I have also made this as mini loaves. I work in the kitchen of an assisted living facility. I am often asked to make the bread for the residents. I usually make four reg size loaves, (9x 5). However, the last time, I used 16 (3x 5) bread tins. I always make 4 batches at one time. Set the Convection oven at 300. These were baked for 25 to 27 minutes. Each mini loaf made 6 or 7 slices. We served 45 ppl two slices each, with a few slices left over

Best banana bread I have ever made! I added 1 cup chopped walnuts, 1 Tbsp cinnamon and 1T vanilla and cut the sugar by 1/4 cup, and it turned out perfectly! Moist on the inside and a a little crispy on the outside. I had to cut baking time by 5 minutes because we have a convection oven. Thank you!

Loved this recipe as a foundation! Made some changes. -Baked at 350 for 50-55 mins. -3/4 cup pecans -Added 1-1.5 tsp cinnamon and vanilla extract for more flavor. -Reduced sugar to 3/4 cup or a little more than 1/2 cup. -Used regular milk and changed to buttermilk by adding 1 tsp vinegar. -Used three medium sized bananas. If your bananas are not brown yet, you can speed up ripening by putting the bananas in the oven for 10 minutes at 350 until nice and brown. Let cool in the freezer for few minutes then start with making the cake. I've experimented with other recipes before, but I believe the buttermilk here creates the ultimate moist cake.

I finally decided to put those lazy good-for-nothing overripe bananas to work! However, I made a few changes, based on the plethora of notes I consumed. First, instead of half a cup of oil, I used 1/4 cup melted butter, and 1/4 cup apple sauce, lightly sweetened. Next, I replaced 1 3/4 cups white sugar with 1/2 cup brown sugar, and 2/3rds cup white sugar. Finally, I added in walnuts to the top of half the loaf's dough/batter, and pecans to the other half. I then gently plunged them down as much as I could, which didn't go too far. Both nut additions were equally tasty! I have a convection oven, so I set my timer for 10 minutes early, but, as you can probably see from my picture, the top browned just a little bit over much. So, next time I bake this tremendously tasty bread, I think I'll take it out on the hour. Both my husband and I LOVED it, though, and I was glad I'd at least rendered it a tad more healthy!

My husband said Yum Yum and so did the grandkids. Everybody loved it. The only thing I did different was, I poured cinnamon and sugar on the bottom and sides of the pan after greasing it. Then I poured the batter into the pan and sprinkled some more cinnamon and sugar on top. Loved it❤️

YUM! I've made the recipe tons of times, just as muffins(you only bake for 20 minutes) and with a few exceptions. I do half brown sugar half white, I add some vanilla and a sprinkle of cinnamon, and depending on how I feel I might do 1/2 cup melted butter instead of oil. They always turn out delicious and moist!
My family loves this recipe out of all the ones I have made. I add chocolate chips instead of pecans. It freezes well.
A little bit sweet for me but fantastic! I would reduce the sugar

This was a really great tasting banana bread that my husband and I both loved. I loved it for the bread itself, but the pecans pushed it over the top for me! Loved the nuts. (I added a bit more than the recipe called for) Delicious.
Perfect recipe; I added a teaspoon of pumpkin pie spice and a teaspoon of vanilla to the batter.
I’ve made a lot of banana bread in my half century of life and this actually IS the best banana bread recipe!! Everyone I have made it for absolutely loves it! Try it as is written!

Added extra banana and made 3 mini loaves... added candied pecans to one, toasted walnuts to another, and poppy seeds with toasted coconut to the third. Per suggestion, split the sugar between white and dark brown. So good!
Delicious! It is the best recipe I’ve ever made.

Title is well deserved! I have a problem following recipes for a myriad of reasons but I'm so glad I did! I followed the recipe exactly and it was worth it! I used my mixer, added all the wet ingredients first, then added the mixed dry ingredients. I add the bananas last. Only difference--I used almond milk and vinegar for the buttermilk. I took the advice of a commenter and drizzled a brown sugar/cinnamon/flour mix on the bottom of the parchment paper and the top of the wet loaf before I put it in. Do NOT tell my grandmother, but it really is the best banana bread recipe lol.

I followed the whole recipe with two tweaks. I didn't have buttermilk, so I subbed with the same amount of milk plus 1/2 tbsp. lemon juice. I don't like the top of my banana bread too brown, so I covered it with aluminum foil halfway through the baking time. Would make again!
